metadata.summary: Daryz looks perfectly placed to defend his Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe crown in four weeks, judged on his dominant display in the Prix Foy.
metadata.content: Daryz warms up for Arc with dominant display in Prix Foy | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to content Daryz warms up for Arc with dominant display in Prix Foy Daryz was given the perfect rehearsal ahead of his bid to retain his crown in the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe with a smooth success in the Prix Foy at Parislongchamp Sunday 6 September 2026 17:53, UK Image: Daryz (M. Barzalona) wins Qatar Prix Foy Gr.2 in ParisLongchamp, France, 06/09/2026, photo: Zuzanna Lupa Daryz looks perfectly placed to defend his Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe crown in four weeks, judged on his dominant display in the Prix Foy. Francis-Henri Graffard's charge made the perfect start to his four-year-old campaign by winning two more Group Ones at his beloved ParisLongchamp, with a comeback victory in the Prix Ganay followed by a runaway triumph in the Prix Aga Khan IV. He could only finish third when sent across the Channel for the Prince of Wales's Stakes at Royal Ascot in June, but with connections feeling they had viable excuses for that below-par run, the son of Sea The Stars was expected to regain winning ways back on home turf. On paper his task was not entirely straightforward, with George Scott's 10-length Coronation Cup winner and fellow Arc aspirant Bay City Roller among his three rivals, and as expected the latter was sent straight to the front by Oisin Murphy in an attempt to draw the sting out of Daryz's exceptional finishing kick. A strong British and Irish contingent went to post for the Group One contest, with Aidan O'Brien's Irish 2,000 Guineas hero Gstaad the hot favourite ahead of Charlie Appleby's Opera Ballo and the Ed Walker-trained Ten Bob Tony. Unlike that trio, Francis-Henri Graffard's Erdenali was unproven in Group One company, but he had looked an exciting prospect in winning his first three starts and was an unlucky loser when third in a Group Three on his most recent outing. With Opera Ballo taken on for the lead by Gstaad's pacemaker Dorset, Appleby's charge was a spent force entering the final furlong, at which stage Erdenali and the shock Queen Anne winner Ten Bob Tony moved up to dispute the lead. messages.text: 19th to victory! Antonelli sensationally wins thrilling Italian GP

metadata.summary: Kimi Antonelli completed a remarkable comeback to win his home Italian Grand Prix from 19th place after a race-long battle against Mercedes team-mate George Russell.
metadata.content: Italian GP: Kimi Antonelli sensationally wins thrilling Monza race from George Russell and Max Verstappen | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Italian GP: Kimi Antonelli sensationally wins thrilling Monza race from George Russell and Max Verstappen Championship leader Kimi Antonelli became the first Italian to win at Monza since 1966 after an incredible drive from 19th to first; Antonelli had stunning pace to come through the field, then later caught George Russell in the closing laps; Max Verstappen claimed his fifth podium of 2026 Nigel Chiu Sports Journalist @NigelCJourno Sunday 6 September 2026 17:09, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Italian Grand Prix Kimi Antonelli completed a remarkable comeback to win his home Italian Grand Prix from 19th place after a race-long battle against Mercedes team-mate George Russell. Antonelli was not expected to contend for victory due to grid penalties for exceeding his engine allocation but stormed through the field early on - in between the red flag for Charles Leclerc's huge crash - and showed tremendous pace to catch Russell on an alternative strategy. The two Mercedes and Max Verstappen pulled clear of the field in the first half of the race, exchanging the lead several times, due to the yoyo style of racing caused by the 2026 power units and the impact of having a slipstream around the long straights at Monza.
